summary: An underdoped YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{7-δ}$ thin film embedded in a tunable terahertz cavity exhibits enhanced superconducting response with increased inferred superfluid weight below $T_c$, accompanied by an upward shift of the superconducting onset temperature. A cavity-coupled model for phase-fluctuating superconductors interprets the effect as cavity-enhanced phase stiffness that suppresses long-wavelength phase fluctuations and shifts the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition to higher temperature.
motivation: In underdoped cuprates, pairing correlations persist above the critical temperature $T_c$ where global phase coherence is lost, suggesting phase fluctuations limit superconductivity. The possibility that cavity-modified electromagnetic environments can stabilize superconducting coherence by suppressing phase-disrupting mechanisms rather than strengthening pairing provides a compelling platform to test cavity control of correlated states.
method: Time-domain terahertz spectroscopy measured the temperature-dependent complex conductivity of a 100 nm YBCO film in a tunable Fabry-Pérot cavity formed by the film and a semi-transparent gold mirror separated by 20–4000 μm, with cavity length adjusted by piezoelectric positioners; complex optical conductivity was extracted using the thin-film Tinkham formalism accounting for full cavity propagation effects.
result: The frequency-averaged imaginary conductivity $\bar{\sigma}_2$ (proportional to superfluid weight) is systematically enhanced below $T_c$ in the cavity, with larger enhancement at shorter cavity lengths (most pronounced for $L=20$ μm); the superconducting onset temperature shifts upward by approximately 1 K in the shortest cavity relative to free space, consistent with cavity-enhanced phase stiffness predicted by a modified XY/BKT model.
